intended_object: For manifolds M and N and a point x ∈ M, the evaluation map from the stalk at x of the sheaf of smooth functions M → N (the germs of smooth maps at x) to N, sending a germ [f]ₓ to f(x). Here it is a morphism in the category of types. This comes from the docstring.
explanation:
`smoothSheaf IM I M N` is defined as the sheaf of the local predicate "is C^∞" given by `contDiffWithinAt_localInvariantProp`. `TopCat.stalkToFiber` for a local predicate is the standard map from the stalk to the fiber. It is induced by the colimit property from evaluation at x on each open neighbourhood. The lemma `ι_evalHom` confirms this: on a section i over U it gives `i.1 ⟨x, _⟩`. So the map sends a germ to its value at x, as the docstring says.

The setting is fully general: any nontrivially normed field, any models with corners, and smoothness ∞. The single universe `u` for M and N is a restriction forced by the category-theoretic sheaf framework, and it is documented in the module header. It is not a loss of generality in the construction itself.

The body is literally the same as `smoothSheaf.eval`; this version is only stated as a morphism ⟶ in `Type u` rather than as a plain function. It therefore faithfully defines the germ evaluation map.
